payload.title: AI Builders Daily · 2026-06-13
payload.summary:
**Labs are tightening the screws**: **Anthropic** admits three **Claude Code** regressions and ships a postmortem; managed agents get self-hosted sandboxes and private **MCP** tunnels; builders are suddenly talking about model access, regulation, and ID gates; meanwhile **Vercel** pushes **HarnessAgent** as the new anti-lock-in play.

**气氛明显变了**；**Anthropic** 先把 **Claude Code** 最近掉链子的三处问题摊开讲清，又把托管 Agent 往企业内网里推，沙箱和 **MCP** 通道都给了；另一边不少人开始盯着准入、监管和 Fable 限制，味道一下就不一样了；产品层面也没闲着，**Vercel** 把 **HarnessAgent** 端上来，摆明了要抢 agent 编排这一层。

**Coding agents keep stretching their leash**: long-horizon automation, token-cost backlash, merge-conflict fatigue, benchmark wars, and founders openly saying the real job is now managing agent fleets; even the hot takes feel more operational than theoretical.

**大家聊的也更务实了**；长任务 agent 终于真能跑起来，但账单、上下文、评审瓶颈、合并冲突这些老问题没消失，只是换了个地方爆；有人在吹基准，有人在骂流程，有人已经让 Codex 连跑四天，像是在试探软件生产的下一套默认设置。

sections.headline: **AI Vibe Check**: coding agents rise, open models wobble, API businesses questioned / **AI 风向复盘**：编码 agent 上位，开源模型动摇，API 生意也被怀疑
sections.body:
The episode frames the last six months as a sharp turn toward long-horizon coding agents that can actually stay useful over extended tasks. Ari says engineers are increasingly shifting from doing the work themselves to managing multiple agents, but warns that easier code generation also creates review bottlenecks and bigger understanding gaps inside codebases.

Rob argues the bigger structural story may be the weakening economics of frontier open-weight AI. He points to signs that major labs may keep their best systems proprietary, while companies under compute pressure start caring far more about token efficiency and cost control. The conversation also floats a provocative possibility: if the crunch continues, top labs may prioritize productized access and hosted inference over broad API openness.

这期最有意思的地方，不是又在喊“agent 时代来了”，而是几个人都把话说得更具体了：能跑长任务的编码 agent 现在确实开始有用了，工程师的角色也在往“带 agent 干活”偏。但代价也很现实，代码产出变快了，评审和理解反而更卡，烂账不会自动消失。

另一条线更狠：前沿开源模型的账，可能快算不过来了。嘉宾基本都在怀疑，真正强的模型会不会越来越少地放权重、越来越多地关进 API 和产品里。再加上 token 成本开始真打到企业预算，讨论已经不是抽象路线之争，而是很赤裸的商业和算力约束。

sections.headline: **Anthropic** details three **Claude Code** regressions and a rollback spree / **Anthropic** 拆解 **Claude Code** 三次退化事故，连做回滚
sections.body:
Anthropic says recent complaints about weaker Claude Code behavior traced back not to the model API, but to three product-layer changes: reducing default reasoning effort, a cache-related bug that repeatedly cleared prior reasoning after idle sessions, and a prompt tweak meant to cut verbosity that ended up hurting coding quality. All three were fixed or reverted by April 20, with subscriber usage limits reset afterward.

The post is valuable because it names the exact failure modes users felt: Claude seeming less intelligent, becoming forgetful and repetitive, and burning usage faster than expected. Anthropic also admits its internal evals and testing initially missed the problems, then notes that **Opus 4.7** could catch one of the offending bugs in back-testing when given full repo context. The subtext is clear: product harness changes can degrade agent quality just as much as model changes can.

这篇后记没绕弯子，直接承认最近不少人骂 **Claude Code** 变差，不是 API 模型层出了锅，主要是产品侧三刀砍偏了：默认推理强度从高调到中、空闲会话的历史推理被 bug 反复清掉、还有一版“少说点”的系统提示把写代码质量也带沟里了。最后都在 4 月 20 日前后修掉或回滚，顺手给订阅用户重置额度。

真正值得看的是它把体感问题说实了：没以前聪明、老忘事、重复、工具调用越来越怪，甚至额度掉得比预期快。更扎眼的是，内部评测一开始还没复现出来。意思很明白：agent 产品的退化，不一定是模型退化，很多时候就是你外面那层 harness 和提示词先把事情搞坏了。

sections.headline: **Managed Agents** split the brain, the hands, and the session / **Managed Agents** 把“大脑、手和会话”彻底拆开
sections.body:
Anthropic’s engineering write-up argues that long-running agents need stable interfaces more than fixed implementations. Their answer is Managed Agents: separate the harness that calls Claude, the sandbox that executes code and tools, and the durable session log that stores everything that happened. That lets containers fail, harnesses restart, and context be reread without treating any single running box like a fragile pet.

The architecture shift also tightens security. Untrusted code no longer runs in the same environment as credentials, and external tool access can flow through vault-backed proxies instead of exposing tokens inside the sandbox. A key design point is that the session is not the context window: context lives durably outside Claude’s immediate prompt and can be sliced back in when needed, which is Anthropic’s answer to long-horizon context loss.

这篇更像是 Anthropic 在公开自己对 agent 基础设施的判断：别再把模型、执行环境、会话记录全塞进一个容器里养“宠物机”了，得拆。它把 harness、sandbox、session log 分开，哪个挂了就换哪个，agent 不该因为一个卡死容器就整段报废。

安全这块也讲得很直白。生成出来的不可信代码，不该跟凭证待在同一个地方；token 要么绑资源，要么放金库，别让 sandbox 直接摸到。还有个关键点挺重要：会话记录不等于上下文窗口。上下文应该在外面持久化，模型需要时再取，不然长任务迟早被窗口长度反噬。

sections.headline: **Claude Managed Agents** adds self-hosted sandboxes and private **MCP** tunnels / **Claude Managed Agents** 新增自托管沙箱和私有 **MCP** 通道
sections.body:
Anthropic is pushing Managed Agents deeper into enterprise territory. Agents can now execute tools inside a sandbox the customer controls, either on their own infrastructure or through providers like **Cloudflare**, **Daytona**, **Modal**, and **Vercel**. Anthropic keeps the orchestration loop, while execution, files, and network controls stay within the customer’s boundary.

The second update is private MCP connectivity. With MCP tunnels, agents can reach internal databases, APIs, and knowledge systems without exposing those services to the public internet. Anthropic’s pitch is straightforward: keep the agent brain hosted, but move the hands and the sensitive network path behind your own perimeter. That is a concrete answer to the biggest enterprise objection to hosted agents.

这次更新就一个方向：把托管 agent 往企业能接受的边界里塞。Anthropic 保留编排和上下文管理，但真正跑工具的沙箱可以放到你自己的基础设施里，或者挂在 **Cloudflare**、**Daytona**、**Modal**、**Vercel** 这些提供方上，文件、网络策略、审计都留在你那边。

另一个点是 **MCP** 通道。它让 agent 直接碰内网里的数据库、私有 API、知识库，不需要把这些服务暴露到公网。说白了，就是“大脑”还在 Anthropic，“手”和敏感连接尽量别出你的边界。对企业客户来说，这比任何概念宣传都更关键。

sections.headline: Maybe **Git** is the next thing to die / 也许下一个该死的是 **Git**
sections.body:
## The Future Codebase

After the PR dies, after the Code Review dies,
i am seriously wondering if Git needs to die next.

roughly 20-40% of code spend is just managing and updating merge conflicts. necessary evil? or legacy "horseless carriage"? cargo culting the past?

we don't do line by line merge conflicts when we collaborate with human colleagues - instead we chat, suggest edits, do side comments, and an owner ships it. 

btw we also don't do CI/CD even collaborating on documents with serious legal/financial implications.

maybe the future codebase looks more like a Notion or Linear database than .git objects. It will be less efficient, but more scalable. exactly the Salty Lesson.

## 未来的代码库

如果 PR 死了，如果 Code Review 死了，
我很认真地在想，下一个是不是该轮到 **Git** 了。

大概 20%-40% 的代码成本，都耗在处理和更新合并冲突上。这是必要之恶？还是一种遗留下来的“无马马车”？是在对过去搞仪式性模仿吗？

我们跟人类同事协作时，并不会逐行处理合并冲突；我们会聊天、提修改建议、写边注，然后由 owner 发版。

顺便说一句，我们在协作文档时也不会搞 CI/CD，哪怕那些文档涉及很严肃的法律或财务问题。

也许未来的代码库会更像 **Notion** 或 **Linear** 数据库，而不是 `.git` 对象。效率可能更低，但扩展性更强。这正是 **Salty Lesson**。

sections.headline: Levie calls model controls a regulatory turning point / Levie 说模型管制是 AI 监管的分水岭
sections.body:
This is a big turning point for AI regulation.

The government is starting to deem some models too powerful for certain uses, which creates a precedent for a range of possible controls in the future.

I’m in the camp that this is unnecessary and we should be primarily regulating the use of AI, as opposed to the underlying models. But, equally, there are plenty of people that actually prefer this outcome.

Either way, it’s unlikely that we’re going back to a world where the government doesn’t have far more meaningful involvement in the rate of AI progress.

这是 AI 监管的一个重大转折点。

政府开始认定，有些模型对某些用途来说太强了，这会为未来一整套可能的控制手段开先例。

我属于另一派：我觉得这没必要，我们更该监管的是 AI 的使用方式，而不是底层模型本身。但同样，也确实有很多人更希望看到这个结果。

不管怎样，想回到那个政府不会更深介入 AI 进展速度的世界，恐怕是不太可能了。

sections.headline: AI tools can scaffold bureaucracy just as fast / AI 工具不只会加速创造，也会加速把流程搭成牢笼
sections.body:
Everyone thinks AI coding tools set founders free.

Watch what people actually build with them: rules, approvals, process, layers. The same cage, assembled faster.

The tool that can scaffold anything in an afternoon will scaffold your bureaucracy in an afternoon too.

Speed of construction is speed of calcification. Build the thing that lets you create new things: experiences that didn’t happen before.

大家都以为 AI 编码工具能把创始人解放出来。

但你看人们实际拿它们搭了什么：规则、审批、流程、层层结构。同一个笼子，只是搭得更快。

那个能让你一下午 scaffold 出任何东西的工具，也能让你一下午把官僚结构 scaffold 完。

建得越快，固化得也越快。去做那种能让你创造新东西的东西，去做以前根本没发生过的体验。

sections.headline: Two voices, one person / 一个人，两个声线
sections.body:
Anyone else have two voices?

I often have two voices that come out both in my writing and how I speak. 

One is the frenetic, time is the enemy, direct, punchy gets to the point quickly and then the second is more calm, measured, structured inquisitive, trying to peel the layers. 

They are distinctive enough that people think it’s two different people (especially in writing). 

They are usually separate but I feel I often oscillate between the two in the same conversation.

还有谁会有两种声音吗？

我经常在写作和说话里都冒出两种不同的声线。

一种很躁，觉得时间是敌人，直接、短促、迅速切到重点；另一种更平静、更克制、更有结构，也更爱追问，想一层层剥开。

它们差异大到别人会以为那是两个人，尤其在文字里更明显。

平时它们通常分开出现，但我感觉自己也常常会在同一场对话里在两者之间来回切。

sections.body:
I can barely keep up with implementing/testing/landing all the Issues/PRs folks submit to https://t.co/qUxn0LF7Ct

Codex runs INSIDE crabbox while it is building crabbox.
This is becoming essential infra for my work.

Codex been looping nonstop for the last 4 days in multiple trees. Since all of it is e2e verifiable it basically builds itself. Codex even signs up for the services automatically via browser/computer use. My main job is adding credit card details and closing things that I don't see as a fit.

我几乎已经跟不上大家往 https://t.co/qUxn0LF7Ct 提的那些 issue 和 PR 的实现、测试、落地速度了。

**Codex** 现在直接跑在 **crabbox** 里面，一边构建 **crabbox** 本身。
这已经快成我工作里的关键基础设施了。

**Codex** 过去 4 天一直在多个代码树里不停循环跑。因为这些东西都能做端到端验证，所以它基本是在自己把自己建出来。**Codex** 甚至还会通过 browser/computer use 自动去注册相关服务。现在我主要干的事，反倒是填信用卡信息，以及把那些我觉得不合适的东西关掉。
